title: First-responder rollout lifeline & pinbook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal checklist and lifeline for first-responder on soft launches/canaries. Small, copyable, and opinionated.
- Keep this as single-pane-of-glass for night shifts where I might be the only eng on call.

Scope:
- Applies to minor model flips, runtime flags, and small-config image updates (no infra-level kernel or OS changes).
- Target: <5% traffic canary -> step to 25% over 2–4 hours if healthy.

High-level rollout plan (one-liner):
1) Pin customers that need stability (customer pin list) -> 2) Launch 1% canary for 30m -> 3) Monitor golden metrics -> 4) Advance by doubling every 30–60m if clean -> 5) Stop/rollback on any hard failure criteria.

Canary schedule (typical):
- T0: 1% traffic, 0 pinned critical customers, 30m observation (fast-path safe).
- T+30m: Check, if good -> 2.5% (or 5% depending on baseline), 60m observation.
- T+90–150m: 10% -> 25% (gradual), then assess for full flip.
- If at any step we see regression we either pin clients or roll back to previous version and run diagnostics.

Cohort definitions (practical):
- GREEN: small internal test tenants + canary cohort (test flags enabled)
- SILVER: low-volume customers (<= 10k monthly requests)
- GOLD: top 20 tenant list (pinned unless we explicitly unpin)
- SHADOW: mirroring traffic for warm caches (no client-visible)

Pinning quick commands (internal CLI):
- pin add --tenant TENANT_ID --version v2026.02.10
- pin list --region us-west1
- pin remove --tenant TENANT_ID (careful: will reflow traffic)
- tip: use --dry-run to validate routing table changes before commit

Key metrics (watch these in order):
1) Error budget burn / 5xx rate (rollout stop threshold: +0.15% absolute or 3x baseline whichever lower)
2) Latency p95 and p99 (stop care if p99 increases by >200ms over baseline)
3) Token-cost delta (unexpected token increase = possible loop/repeat issue)
4) Throughput / concurrency anomalies (backpressure signs)
5) Client-specific anomalies (single-tenant spike in errors)
6) Business KPI quick-checks (checkout failures for commerce customers, search relevance drop signals)

Hard rollback criteria (immediate action):
- Any sustained service-level error increase beyond thresholds above for >5 minutes.
- One customer in GOLD cohort with degradation affecting production flows (immediately pin and roll back).
- Unsafe safety signals: hallucination increases on monitored eval prompts beyond guardrail (see eval-set: rel_canary_v2).

Soft stop / hold criteria (pause & investigate):
- Small transient p99 bump but no user-visible errors -> hold at current fraction for 1–2 cycles, increase TTL for caches.
- Token-cost spike without errors -> investigate prompt loop or sampling parameter drift.

Observability checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Open dashboard: model-route overview + per-tenant p99, error heatmap.
- Confirm tracing is attached for canary requests (trace id sample present).
- Confirm KV cache hit-rate is within expected range (watch warmup slope).
- Post a short note in #release-notifications with rollout fraction and link to dashboards.

First-responder immediate playbook (copyable):
1) Identify: what fraction, which model, what config changed.
2) Snapshot routing: `route show --json > /tmp/route-snapshot.json`
3) Take action: pin critical tenants using CLI (see commands).
4) If rollback: `release rollback --to-version v2026.02.02 --force` (expect warmup lag ~3–5m).
5) Notify: #release-notifications + affected slack channels, mention SRE and Release PM.

Post-rollout observation window (24–72h):
- Keep the canary cohort in a watchlist for 24h after 100% flip.
- Run the small eval harness at +1h, +6h, +24h with representative prompts (script: tools/evals/run_rel_smoke.sh).
- Check business KPIs at +6h and +24h.

Notes-to-self (lessons / shorthand):
- When in doubt: pin first -> investigate -> rollback only if pin insufficient. Pinning is cheap and reversible.
- If a single tenant spikes errors, narrow by client-affinity header and isolate in the gateway to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Watch for background rehydration: warm caches = temporary token delta; correlate with cache-miss histogram.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Still need a reliable presignaling hook for clients to opt-out of canaries (REL-4189).
- Build a small smoke checker that runs three eval prompts on every canary request path (low overhead).
- Confirm that rollback artifacts keep older runtime images for at least 48h.

Quick debugging commands (cheats):
- tail logs for model node: `k logs -l app=runtime-node --since=10m`
- show active routes: `rctl routes --env prod --filter canary`
- check p99 by tenant: `telemetry query "p99(latency) by tenant" --since 30m`

End-of-shift handoff snippet (what to paste into slide/email):
- What I did: launched v2026.02.10 -> 1% -> 5% (no hard failures)
- Current state: at 25% with GOLD tenants pinned; watchlist: tenant:acme-inc elevated p99 by 40ms, non-urgent
- Recommended next steps: hold cadence for 60m, run eval harness at +1h, consider moving to 50% if clean

Random heuristics that have worked:
- Prefer 30–60m observation windows for any fractional change <10%; longer (90m+) if customer-affecting.
- Always verify trace sampling for canary requests before increasing fraction. No traces -> blind escalation.

Small checklist to copy into Slack when launching: 
- Launch note: model v2026.02.10 -> 1% canary -> dashboards: <link> -> pinned: GOLD list -> responders: @oncall-sre @lucia

Scratch follow-ups (action items for me):
- Wire up demo tenants for faster manual smoke runs (low priority).
- Add a short runbook snippet for token-cost anomalies to run automatically when delta>20%

-- lucia
(If this helps, merge into the shared playbook and then delete — but keep local copy for weird nights)
